Messages.Author: Jason Burke
Messages.Body:
Holy Cow Corrupter,

I dont think I've seen a message from you yet that doesnt mention
your tournament rules or NL/GT. Now I agree that Weeny Vote Decks are a
real problem, and that they do force the whole table to gang up on the
offending player, but in my opinion that's the game. I think that the
DCI tournament rules (before they caved to pressure from this group) was
a reasonable answer to this problem. After all the easiest way to take
care of a problem with a CCG is to limit overpowered cards (Legends of
the 5 rings is a good example of this.). Weeny vote decks are not
unbeatable as you seem to suggest, though difficult not unbeatable. I
can think of a few viable answers to WVD/P, but I think that your GT's
are similar to throwing the baby out with the bathwater. Also, I cant
really agree that fortitude loops are infinate, and I would really like
to see a deck design that will consistantly pull of this infinate loop
that you keep outlining in your posts. Please dont take this as a flame,
since it's not intended as such. I respect your views on this subject,
but I simply dont agree that it's a situation that reguires a whole
restructuring of the rules.

Laters...Jason

Messages.Author: The Corrupter
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 11 Aug 1996, Jason Burke wrote:

> I dont think I've seen a message from you yet that doesnt mention
> your tournament rules or NL/GT.

Well, at least you've noticed them then... :)
(As a slight defense, there are quite a few, but with two threads going
on regarding WVP and Repeat Actions, NL/GT are going to come up a lot,
and with it, SPTR)

>Now I agree that Weeny Vote Decks are a

> real problem, and that they do force the whole table to gang up on the

> offending player, ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Note this point...

> but in my opinion that's the game.

That may be the current game state, but that doesn't make it right. Why
should one or two strategies out of a near infinite set cause this
problem, and no others? One of my definitions of "degeneracy" is that if
a deck causes a _consistent_ change in the prey/predator relationship
(i.e, the table needs to deal with it or else), that is a problem.
Certainly, any deck can be in an excellent situation where the table
needs to gang-attack it, but if this is a consistent factor, something is
wrong.

> I think that the
> DCI tournament rules (before they caved to pressure from this group) was
> a reasonable answer to this problem. After all the easiest way to take
> care of a problem with a CCG is to limit overpowered cards (Legends of
> the 5 rings is a good example of this.).

Due note, however, that DCI does not do anything to solve WVP.

> Weeny vote decks are not

> unbeatable as you seem to suggest, though difficult not unbeatable.

I have never claimed that they are undeatable. I do claim that they will
win a disproportionate amount of games, with minimal thought, minimal
skill, and minimal deck construction effort. I do claim WVP virtually
requires an odd environment (everyone playing intercept, for example ;)
or that decks are tailored to beat it. Once we get into Magic style
strategy (The How do I beat Necro? How do I beat Willowgeddon? style
deck construction) and away from how do I defend against the basics, I
think this is a loss to the game. In NL/GT, one can make any deck with
only one real consideration for defense that must be made: how do I stop
the basic strategies (bleed/vote/combat).

> I
> can think of a few viable answers to WVD/P, but I think that your GT's
> are similar to throwing the baby out with the bathwater.

I'm sure many would agree with you. As it stands however, there are few
alternatives:

Vote Pushing Alternate Solutions (instead of only 1 PA per PA):
- Percent Restriction (Adds a number of problems, but holds back WVP)
- 2CL on damaging votes (look, even 4CL doesn't stop WVP)
- Do nothing (live in a broken environment)

No Repeat Action Alternate Solutions (only attempt once...):
- No repeat of specific action (basicly the same thing)
- No repeat of a successful action (allows Majestic bleed problems)
- Add more to the restricted list, lower the Restricted CL to 4 or 5
(problems that have already been gotten into, what about non-degenerate
uses of those cards)

Are those much better?

> Also, I cant

> really agree that fortitude loops are infinate, and I would really like
> to see a deck design that will consistantly pull of this infinate loop

> that you keep outlining in your posts.

Try playing one of them. I can resend it to you.

> Please dont take this as a flame,
> since it's not intended as such. I respect your views on this subject,
> but I simply dont agree that it's a situation that reguires a whole
> restructuring of the rules.

I don't take it as a flame... As it says in my .sig, Comments?

Differences of opinion are a good thing, it causes discussion. Various
discussions on Jyhad have shifted me from a XCL to a 10%CL to NL to NL/GT
player. I have seen many people make the transition with me. In other
subjects, the same thing happens. If I am right (which of course, we all
think we are :), hopefully I can change some opinions. If not, hopefully
someone will convince me. It won't be the first time.

Not to take the wind out of your sails, but if the DCI "fixes" one of their
own rules (e.g., changing the 2-card restricted list to a 6-card), then that
rule must have really been broken. The DCI is even less apt to overturn
a rule than the RT. If they say it's broken, believe them. (This doesn't
apply to the DCI's "fixes" of normal rules (like deck construction) - if they
fix on of those, it's most likely just a MtG-style reflex).

>Personally I dont agree with either (CL or GT), but I agree less with GT
>simply because I find rules addendum to be very annoying (just a person quirk
>I guess. I find house rules to be even more annoying. =). My last play group
>didnt play with any limits, but somehow no one in the group ever tried or wanted
>to play a weeny vote deck, though the use of majesties was pretty heavy.

Then how do you feel about Cross Table Bleeds (a rules addendum to both
Jyhad and V:tES)? Card Limits are no less of a rules addendum than GT.
The rules state how decks are constructed and how actions are taken. Changing
either of these is a change in the rules.

I have heard this arguement at conventions many times. The next sentence
I hear is usually the one you give below:

> The only environment where this isnt necessarly true is durring tournaments.
> For regular game play people should make their decks anyway they want,
> and not be subject to CL's (which are silly, IMO, for friendly play).

The idea of the "social problem" is that people playing in friendly
groups just shouldn't make those big, bad mean decks, after all, they
aren't friendly. People that make them for friendly play just shouldn't,
and if they do, they have a problem.

The whole idea above is ludicrous.

In NL/GT, no one is going to ask you to play a deck because it is "too
tough". No one is going to be miffed if you play S&B because it is
"unfair" (though they might be bored by the game. S&B is notoriously
unexciting, whether winning or losing). You can play, fully confident in
the idea that your deck, however good or bad, can be played in a "friendly"
environment. WVP, if/when played, can be viable in NL/GT, but it hardly
makes the table gang up on it. No such deck exists (or at least no one
has stepped forward in all the time I have had my challenge issued.
Remember, $50 to (the first) someone who can come up with a degenerate NL/GT
deck.)

> Unfortunately the new play group that im in (I recently moved), plays
> with the first version of the tournament rules (2CL on restricted, and
> 6CL on everything else.).

<Quibble> There has never been a set of tourneyment rules that you

There is a definate problem here. You were being beaten by WVP, and so
in answer, you pulled out your anti-WVP deck and (of course) slaughtered
the WVPer. Playing certain decks to beat other decks to make them play
something else is not really all that fun, though it does (eventually)
cause a change in the deck they play (and thus increase fun), the idea
that this problem even springs up is bad. Under NL/GT, you don't have to
hope someone is playing a degenerate deck.

> > Due note, however, that DCI does not do anything to solve WVP.

> Not anymore, but it did at first.

With a TWO-card limit on damage votes. Great fix. :p

> > I have never claimed that they are undeatable. I do claim that they will

> > skill, and minimal deck construction effort. I do claim WVP virtually
> > requires an odd environment (everyone playing intercept, for example ;)

> > the basic strategies (bleed/vote/combat).

> Herein lies the arguement between us, I dont see "Magic Style strategy" as
> a problem, in fact the social mechanics inherit in this strategy is inherit
> in all CCG's.

Propblem: When a game requires people not play with certain aspects of it
(WVP, for example) because playing that way breaks the game balance, that
is Bad. This is akin to saying in chess, "Oh, you can do whatever
you want, but we'd really like it around here if you don't play Queen's
Gambit, because that is too difficult to beat". If this were the case in
chess, the game would no longer be played, because the game would be
obviously flawed and limited (respond to Queen's Gambit only). Instead
the rules set allows Chess to be an excellent game, where any
opening/response that is done is allowed, and no opening is disallowed in
friendly play as "too powerful". The Golden Tenets house rules make the
total Jyhad Rules set an even playing field (though, of course, certain
card rulings might be cosmetically better, they aren't game breakers).

> It's a part of CCG's that I truely love (It's what keeps me
> playing them, instead of Necromunda. =). Though I think that no matter what
> degenerate decks come into play, eventualy everyone gets back to the basics.

Isn't it better to never have a degenerate deck?

On Fri, 16 Aug 1996, Anise Sorghum wrote:

> I've seen a large amount of commentary on this. I do agree with the

> type. However, with that said, has anyone else had success with Elder
> Kindred Network + Kindred Coercion? Both are faintly useful in their
> own right, but the combination has been quite amusing when there are
> multiple Caitiff princes.

I was running one at a SPTR-Jyhad tournament. It was a Ventrue
Reactionary vote deck, throwing out cards that allowed others to vote to
destroy them (Elysium, Anarch Revolt, etc.) and cards to keep people
other than my prey alive (Life Boon, Parity Shift, etc.). The best I was
able to do was against a Weenie Vote Push prey, who I caused 11 (???)
pool damage in turn 2. (He called a KRC which I allowed, and then called
a Praxis Seizure with his 2nd of 3 vamps. My two vamps (Gideon and
Violette) Dread Gazed and Surprise Influenced. I ousted him, though I
didn't make it to the finals (the WVP did).

As an aside, that tournament was relatively interesting (re: the WVP
deck). The first game the WVPer was in, he swept the table in 20 (!!!)
minutes. The next game, I ousted him rather quickly. I saw him later
stalled out against someone's Brujah vote deck at another table.
Apparently, in the finals, he only barely managed to get his first Praxis
Seizure vote passed, in return for supporting the next 3 votes of a
player acrossed the table. His prey (a run-away Sneaky Intercept deck
(+1 to +2 stealth, +1 to +2 intercept, escape combat cards and light
bleeds)), was holding down some of the damaging votes, but the WVP deck got
killed acrossed the table by the guy who he promised to help (First vote,
Dramatic Upheaval, 2nd two votes Conservative Agitation). Around here,
deals are stuck by for fear of losing dealmaking ability in future games.
A Good final game. The man who won (the Dramatic Upheavel deck) was
playing a better version of my anti-vote deck (less focused on
anti-votes, and more focused on forcing people to call the votes he
wanted or else), and won by _withdrawing_.

Again, a good final game.

Jason Burke <jbu...@weldnet.com> wrote:

>The Corrupter wrote:
>> I have never claimed that they are undeatable. I do claim that they will
>> win a disproportionate amount of games, with minimal thought, minimal
>> skill, and minimal deck construction effort. I do claim WVP virtually
>> requires an odd environment (everyone playing intercept, for example ;)
>> or that decks are tailored to beat it. Once we get into Magic style
>> strategy (The How do I beat Necro? How do I beat Willowgeddon? style
>> deck construction) and away from how do I defend against the basics, I
>> think this is a loss to the game. In NL/GT, one can make any deck with
>> only one real consideration for defense that must be made: how do I stop
>> the basic strategies (bleed/vote/combat).

>Herein lies the arguement between us, I dont see "Magic Style strategy" as
>a problem, in fact the social mechanics inherit in this strategy is inherit
>in all CCG's. It's a part of CCG's that I truely love (It's what keeps me
>playing them, instead of Necromunda. =). Though I think that no matter what
>degenerate decks come into play, eventualy everyone gets back to the basics.

Well... having been an extremely good MtG player for a while now, and
playing continually against one of the best (George Baxter), I have to
say I personally think the MtG system sucks. Looking at a deck and
saying... will this beat necro, will this beat white weenie, will this
beat willowgeddon, will it beat howling bind... is bad. In Jyhad
decks can be designed to deal with only the basic strategies, and not
have to worry will it be Setite bleed or will it be Malk bleed. I can
just worry about bleed decks.
And as far as "Everyone getting back to the basics." Thats not true,
in a tournament setting, which is (I believe) the main thing many of
us are worried about. I want to see VTES tourneys as big as MtG ones
(well at least before the protour), and I'd like to see the same for
NetRunner. This isn't going to happen with there are decks that will
win too often. The only reason MtG hasn't been killed by the current
near dominance of Necro is that fact that its so popular and people
have spend so much money that they will not let it die.
In a friendly setting, no one is going to play WVP to the extreme that
it will happen in tourneys. There will be certain favorite decks that
everyone will probably start to slant against, and that will affect
design (I know it has for me), but in general people are just trying
to have fun. Heck even after just playing WVP 2 times in my group, I
still here comments to the effect of "I hope you're playing your WVP,
I have my deck set up to kill that dead." Why are they still thinking
about the 2 times I played it (and only did well once mind you) if it
isn't a broken strategy. On the other hand, I've played Brujah combat
at least 8 times, and no one has ever said something similar about
that (and won 2 times I believe).

>>
>> Vote Pushing Alternate Solutions (instead of only 1 PA per PA):
>> - Percent Restriction (Adds a number of problems, but holds back WVP)
>> - 2CL on damaging votes (look, even 4CL doesn't stop WVP)
>> - Do nothing (live in a broken environment)

>Personally I like the last alternative. Though if there had to be a rules
>change I would rather see Vote Pushing changed then GT implimented. Vote
>pushing is degenerate to begin with since it allows advantages that arent
>afforded to other deck designs, hand cycling to be specific. But this is
>a different argument. (I kinda thought that the tap to push a vote was
>one of the best alternative.)

To me, fixing vote push would be a huge step in the right direction.
I'm for no vote push, with or without GT wrapped around it. I think
it solves one of the base problems with voting... the ability to cycle
cards like crazy if needed. Another ok solution is you can only push
with vote cards if you have to... as in already used all on the table
votes (from vampires) and you are still going to lose the vote, push
as much as needed to get ahead.

Whoops... time to get back to woirk (on a Saturday no less... sheesh)

Charles

Messages.Body:
Charles T. Schwope wrote:

<A whole lot snipped>

<< Another ok solution is you can only push
with vote cards if you have to... as in already used all on the table
votes (from vampires) and you are still going to lose the vote, push
as much as needed to get ahead.>>

Ok I'll admit this is taken out of context, but I really like the idea.
I wonder why I never thought of this before. I do not like Golden Tenets.
I've been playing them in JOL and they aren't bad, but there are times when
I haven't been able to do whats best for my game because of no repeat
actions. I have been playing with no house rules No Limits and No Problems
for some time now so I don't see the need for GT. But since everyone seems
so caught up in Vote Push as a card cycling method, why not try only pushing
votes as much as is needed. You can't add intercept or stealth if you don't
need it so why should you be able to add votes when they aren't needed. On the
other hand, if the votes are needed I see no reason that they shouldn't be
allowed to be pushed.

This creates hand jams in VP decks like not intercepting a stealth deck creates
hand jams of stealth cards. The stealth deck in GT is allowed to cycle stealth
cards if it needs to beat intercept and should be allowed to since it put effort
into making sure there would be stealth when it was needed, but by the same effect
that vote deck has vote cards that it would have (as needed only)put effort to
ensure that it is able to do what it is designed to.

I am sure that most of the GT warriors out there have already thought of this in
some form and dismissed it as insufficient, but hey if you can't push in politics
why should you be able to push stealth everytime to get your malks seven bleeds
through.

In any case I still won't implement it unless it becomes official, and I doubt I
will ever implement GT even if it does become official (there are just some rules
I don't like--I still don't like the official ruling on Rostrecht, but I use it
for consistency), but I guess I would have to start making house rules if GT
became the official way. Bath water and babies and blood on the mantle and all
that :)

Anyway thanks for listening--

jon

Jonathan G. Sushinsky (su...@wam.umd.edu) wrote:

: cards if it needs to beat intercept and should be allowed to since it put effort
: into making sure there would be stealth when it was needed, but by the same effect
: that vote deck has vote cards that it would have (as needed only)put effort to
: ensure that it is able to do what it is designed to.

Our group currently uses this fix on voting, and there are some good and
bad sides to it. Yes, it does prevent a vote deck from card-cycling, but
it brings up a whole other raft of problems...

Several of the cards in the current card set are designed _specifically_
with the idea that they may pass or fail by a large number of votes; Elder
Kindred Network is one, Voter Captivation is another. If the vote can
only be pushes until it is exactly tied (in case of a failed vote) or
winning by exactly one, then both of these cards lose much of their
efficacy.

Another problem is this: if a person has both titled vamps and vote cards
in their hands, you _still_ cannot stop them from cycling.

Example: Three other players at the table, no vote decks. Prey has out a
prince and a primogen, another prince lies elsewhere at the table.
Someone else has the Edge. I am playing a vote/bleed deck, and have out
two princes.

I throw down a KRC aimed at my prey, and the other guy with a prince. (my
grand-prey). Between them, they see that they have enough votes to stop
me, _if_ I do not have any further vote cards in my hand (and with a
reasonably-made vote/bleed deck, it could happen).

Possible votes against: 6. Visible votes for: 4 + vote card.

Prey votes against me with primogen. I throw down a vote card. 2-1 for me.
They still have enough to tie, including the edge... Prey votes with his
prince too. I throw out two more vote cards.

Vote is now 4-3 in my favour, but only three votes remain on the table
in possible opposition, while my two princes still have not voted. Unless
someone else can come up with at _least_ two hidden votes, I can't lose
this. No further votes - vote passes. I just cycled three cards, and
still had 4 votes left 'in reserve'.

But wait! Say I _do_ have a Voter Captivation. Can I use my Princes to
vote now? Or are they not allowed to voice an opinion on a vote that is
already passing?

Just to say that it is not _quite_ as simple as the original proposition
would make it seem, and I'd be interested to hear how Mr. Schwope's group
got around these problems. (Sadly, our group hasn't played much since
three of us all got new jobs about 2 months ago...)

Still using Nicole's account...

On Mon, 19 Aug 1996, Jonathan G. Sushinsky wrote:

> Charles T. Schwope wrote:

> <A whole lot snipped>

> << Another ok solution is you can only push
> with vote cards if you have to... as in already used all on the table
> votes (from vampires) and you are still going to lose the vote, push
> as much as needed to get ahead.>>

This has been suggested before, works relatively well, but has the
adverse affect of suddenly making WVP become a threat again...

> Ok I'll admit this is taken out of context, but I really like the idea.
> I wonder why I never thought of this before.

It has. In my playtesting with a local playgroup, it made WVP just
barely less viable than pure Jyhad (w/ pushing rules).

> I do not like Golden Tenets.
> I've been playing them in JOL and they aren't bad, but there are times when
> I haven't been able to do whats best for my game because of no repeat
> actions. I have been playing with no house rules No Limits and No Problems
> for some time now so I don't see the need for GT.

Likely because you haven't seen someone _try_ to break the spirit of the
game through the rules. A game is flawed if it can be stretched like a
NL non-GT game can. Repeat actions allow Freaky Bleed, Infinite Gangrel,
and other problems. Vote Pushing allows WVP, unfair card cycling for
voters, and makes vote decks in general have an easy time of passing
votes (as compared to other decks having to work at their strategy more
for a payoff). So far, no one has been able to break NL/GT.

> But since everyone seems
> so caught up in Vote Push as a card cycling method, why not try only pushing
> votes as much as is needed. You can't add intercept or stealth if you don't
> need it so why should you be able to add votes when they aren't
> needed. On the other hand, if the votes are needed I see no reason
> that they shouldn't be allowed to be pushed.

It creates the WVP phenomena, albeit at only 95% as compared to 100%
strength.

> This creates hand jams in VP decks like not intercepting a stealth
> deck creates hand jams of stealth cards. The stealth deck in GT is
> allowed to cycle stealth cards if it needs to beat intercept and
> should be allowed to since it put effort into making sure there would
> be stealth when it was needed, but by the same effect that vote deck
> has vote cards that it would have (as needed only)put effort to
> ensure that it is able to do what it is designed to.

This is totally untrue. A stealth card without anyone trying to
intercept you is a dead card in your hand. It does, literally, nothing.
An unpushed vote card can be used in the next action on its own merits.

> I am sure that most of the GT warriors out there have already thought
> of this in some form and dismissed it as insufficient,

Yes.

> but hey if you
> can't push in politics why should you be able to push stealth everytime
> to get your malks seven bleeds through.

Different analogy altogether. Your statement (though I believe in just,
or as an arguement ad absurdium) nullifies the entire stealth/intercept
portion of the game. The stopping of vote pushing does nothing at all
similar.

> In any case I still won't implement it unless it becomes official, and
> I doubt I will ever implement GT even if it does become official

I hope you don't mind playing in an environment that can be broken as
soon as someone decides they want to do it...

> (there are just some rules I don't like--I still don't like the
> official ruling on Rostrecht, but I use it for consistency),

I don't like that ruling either. Our playgroup doesn't use it, unless
someone runs a tourney.

> but I guess I would have to start making house rules if GT
> became the official way. Bath water and babies and blood on the
> mantle and all that :)

Its funny hearing the "baby and bathwater" analogy that's sprung up
lately. Everyone that plays GT and finds themselves _occasionally_ not
being able to do everything they want to uses the analogy, despite the fact
that the overall strategy of their deck is almost not affected at all (In JOL6,
one player had to wait a turn before recruiting another retainer. He did
some other action in his deck instead) and that it completely curtails
degeneracy. I guess I'd prefer playing in a non-degenerate setting to
being able to occasionally bring out 2 Raven Spies in a turn, or bleed
with the same minion twice.
